Derrière Naufragés — une histoire vraie,: Behind Naufragés — une histoire vraie ("Castaways — a true story"), formerly In Extremis, histoires de survie, is Daniel Fiévet. A France Inter journalist and producer for years, with a scientific background, and above all a voice and tone made for storytelling — the essential ingredients to carry an audience along, as we'd already seen with Le Grand Récit (episode 30).
Fiévet n'est pas un aventurier — il n'a: Fiévet isn't an adventurer — he probably hasn't survived anything more dramatic than a delayed high-speed train. But he tells other people's survival stories with a precision that makes you feel you're there. 45-minute episodes, one true story each time, from the 18th century to the present day: mountains, sea, jungle, desert… and even space, with Apollo 13.
Ce n'est pas un homme derrière un micro: It isn't a man behind a mic reading a text: Fiévet's narration, voice-overs for the characters, sound effects, music. Somewhere between documentary and film. Close your eyes and you're in the storm — or falling into a crevasse.
Temperatures, distances, exact times. This level of precision turns each episode into a physical experience: you're hot, you're cold, you're thirsty, you're scared. From your sofa. That's the magic of storytelling.
Joe Simpson, alpiniste tombé dans une cr: Joe Simpson, the climber who fell into a crevasse in the Andes, whose partner cut the rope thinking he was dead — and who dragged himself for miles with a broken leg. Ingrid Betancourt, six years a FARC hostage in the jungle. Hugh Glass, the trapper mauled by a grizzly and left for dead, who travelled hundreds of kilometres to find those who'd abandoned him (the story of The Revenant).
Une référence forte du podcast narratif: A strong reference in narrative podcasting in France. Daniel Fiévet pulls off something difficult: bringing historical stories to life. You don't listen to the past, you live it. And you come out of each episode with sincere gratitude for your everyday comfort — along with a slight paranoia about outdoor activities.
Seule réserve : le format 45 minutes dem: The only reservation: the 45-minute format requires settling in, the opposite of short formats. But the tension never drops, and the editing has a lot to do with it. The only real risk is never wanting to leave your flat again.
« Scénario : tu tombes dans une crevasse: “Scenario: you fall into a crevasse, broken leg, your partner cuts the rope. — I stay in the crevasse and make ice lollies. It's quiet, nobody to bother me, I reflect on my life choices.” — Lolo, whom In Extremis mostly proves was right to stay home
